div.head: III Atr 4.2
div.ab: And gif se ágena frígia nelle þæt ordal gesecean, gilde XX óran, ⁊ sy his spæce forlóren; ⁊ he þeah gange þam landrícan to ordale oððe agife twygilde.
Et si agenfria uenire nolit ad ordalium uidendum, reddat uiginti oras et perdat placitum suum; et ille tamen eat landesrico (id est terre domino) ad ordalium uel reddat duplum.
And gif se ágena frígia nelle þæt ordal gesecean, gilde XX óran ⁊ sy his spæce forlóren; ⁊ he þeah gange þam landrícan to ordale oððe agife twygilde.

Und wenn der Eigenthümer zum Ordal [als Kläger] zu kommen unterlässt, büsse er [dem Herrn] 20 Ör, und sei seine Klage verloren; und jener schreite dennoch für den Immunitätsherrn zum Ordal oder zahle [diesem] doppelt [den gestohlenen Werth].

And if the owner fails to come to the ordeal [as plaintiff], let him pay [the lord] 20 ores, and let his suit be lost; and let that [accused] nevertheless go to the ordeal on behalf of the lord of the immunity, or pay [him] double [the stolen value].

But if the owner [of the goods] shall fail to appear at the ordeal, he shall pay 20 ores and shall lose his case. But nevertheless the lord of the manor shall cause him (the thief) to go to the ordeal or to pay double the value of the goods.
And if the owner will not attend the ordeal, he is to pay 20 ores, and his suit shall be lost; and yet he [the accused] is to go to the ordeal for the lord of the estate, or to pay two-fold.

note.seg: Q, der agendfrio (s. d. Wb) mehrfach nicht versteht, scheint geseccan flüchtig mit geseon zu vermengen
Q, who repeatedly fails to understand agendfrio (see that word in Wb), seems hastily to confuse geseccan with geseon

‘before’ versteht Price-Thorpe; allein dies gilt nur bisweilen, wenn der Immunitätsherr zugleich Herr des Wapentake war und nicht einen Vogt diesem vorgesetzt hatte. Dem Gesetzgeber kommt hier darauf an, wer das Geld empfängt, nicht wer das Ordal leitet.—Der Beweis (s. d. 6a) wird hier dem Richter erbracht, da der Kläger ausgeblieben ist

Price-Thorpe understand ‘before’; but this holds only sometimes, when the lord of the immunity was at the same time lord of the wapentake and had not set a reeve over it. What matters to the legislator here is who receives the money, not who conducts the ordeal. — The proof (see that word 6a) is here furnished to the judge, since the plaintiff has failed to appear
Da Klage verloren (Schreuer 41), muss dies Strafgeld sein; s. o. 3, 4²
Since the claim is lost (Schreuer 41), this must be a fine; see above 3, 4²
þam landrican is probably to be taken as dativus commodi. A more literal translation would be, ‘he (the thief) is to go to the ordeal for (the benefit of) the lord of the manor.’
Presumably to the lord of the manor.
